plan.answer:
Start by keeping each weighed portion separate and planning two kept-separate blends that differ only in share of stream A, because that shows whether variation follows A-share without guessing about strength. You can do the weighing, sorting and labelling at home with your scale; moulding specimens and running the strength method needs a suitable facility that is not confirmed.

To do this you need your portion weighing records, one chosen A-share level to aim for first, and the single specimen shape and method you will count for your strength screen. Use the trial-composition balancing tool to work out how much of each stock gives each chosen share, and share polymer identity and additive information with any facility before heated work.

material_routes.title: Set A-share with stock B
material_routes.change: Adjust share of variable stream A by blending with stock B, keeping preparation and process fixed within the comparison.
material_routes.why: Changing only A-share may show whether strength variation tracks the variable stream, without guessing mixture behaviour.
steps: Use your home scale to weigh stream A and stock B for each lot.
Prepare two kept-separate lots that differ only in A-share, for example your entered 250 g A plus 750 g B portion as one level and a lower-A level.
Use the trial-composition balancing tool to set the weights for the chosen share.
Label each lot with weights and A-share and keep identities fixed.
tradeoffs: More levels means more specimens and test cost.
Lower-A blends use more of stock B.
Home weighing cannot show strength; facility moulding and testing are still needed.
material_routes.check: Mould specimens by one fixed process at a suitable facility and test to: Material strength screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using one stated specimen and method.

material_routes.title: Sort and prepare A first
material_routes.change: Change preparation of stream A before blending, keeping A-share fixed within the comparison.
material_routes.why: More consistent feed may help consistent moulding and a clearer strength comparison when moisture and contamination effects are unknown.
steps: Sort stream A to remove obvious non-PE pieces and record what was removed.
Clean and dry as space allows and record dampness and treatment per lot.
Blend sorted A with B at the same A-share as an unsorted control where useful.
tradeoffs: Extra labour, space and drying time.
Sorting may reduce usable amount of A.
material_routes.check: Compare lots at the same A-share by sorting record and moulding behaviour, then by: Material strength screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using one stated specimen and method.

engineering_routes.title: Sleeve shape for easier handling
engineering_routes.change: Revise cover shape to lower stress in handling while keeping material identities and process fixed for comparison.
engineering_routes.why: Handling loads can be carried more by shape than by higher yield stress, which may help when input varies.
steps: Keep function split: inner pot holds soil and water, cover is a decorative sleeve with clearance and a gap so water is not trapped.
Add shape stiffness as adjustable design choices, for example rolled rim, ribs and draft, without changing A/B identities.
Make a flat paper template to explore footprint and clearance with your inner pots.
tradeoffs: Ribs or thicker walls may use more material and need a different mould, not confirmed.
Paper template answers footprint and clearance only; it does not prove drainage, stiffness or strength.
engineering_routes.check: Check fit and handling with the inner pot using real geometry; strength still needs: Material strength screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using one stated specimen and method. Fit, handling and outdoor durability need their own separate targets and short outdoor time does not prove durability.

engineering_routes.title: Traceable lots ready for facility
engineering_routes.change: Keep portions traceable and prepare weighed lots at home, defer moulding and testing to a suitable facility.
engineering_routes.why: Keeping A-share separate preserves a valid comparison and keeps a useful preparation decision ready without assuming processing is available.
steps: Keep each raw portion and each trial blend labelled with its A and B weights and date.
Weigh trial blends at home; do not mould at home.
Ask a facility about moulding, specimen preparation and the stated tensile method; none is confirmed so this plan does not mean production can start.
Provide polymer and additive information to the facility before any heated processing.
tradeoffs: Facility time and specimen testing add cost and delay.
engineering_routes.check: Check scale capability and uncertainty is suited to the weight differences between lots; display steps alone do not prove accuracy. Strength still needs: Material strength screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using one stated specimen and method.

Prepare two labelled lots: different A-share with same preparation, or same A-share with different preparation; change one variable only.
Confirm a facility for moulding and the single stated specimen and tensile method, and provide material identity information before heated work.
Make a paper template for cover footprint and clearance with your inner pots while facility testing is pending.

Strength still needs moulding by one fixed process at a suitable facility and testing to: Material strength screen: tensile yield stress at least 25 MPa, using one stated specimen and method. Fit, handling and outdoor durability need their own separate observations, with no batch-wide pass or dose-response inferred from the synthetic points.
